debug_info.ori_prompt: A single friendly cartoon ant, dark reddish-brown color, centered on a warm cream background. The ant has exactly six legs, two antennae with small round tips, two large round friendly eyes, a small smile, and three clearly segmented body parts (head, thorax, abdomen). Soft-clay 3D picture-book illustration style: rounded plump segments, thick warm dark-brown outline (not black), soft directional studio lighting from the upper-left at 45 degrees creating a soft highlight and gentle shadow, subtle soft shadow underneath, no gradients beyond soft light-to-shadow falloff, no text, no watermark, no additional objects, high-quality children's book illustration, anatomically correct insect with six legs, 1:1 square composition, plenty of whitespace around the subject, side-view or three-quarter view standing pose.
debug_info.actual_prompt:
A high-quality 3D rendered soft-clay picture-book illustration in a warm, friendly children's book aesthetic, the overall color palette built around a smooth warm cream background — the kind of creamy off-white that feels like freshly kneaded fondant, completely clean and uncluttered, with generous whitespace breathing room on all four sides of the composition, the ant centered precisely within a 1:1 square frame occupying roughly one-third to one-half of the total image area, every corner of the cream background left intentionally open and pristine, no props, no text, no watermarks, no additional objects anywhere in the frame.

The single ant subject is rendered in a three-quarter side-view standing pose, body oriented at approximately forty-five degrees toward the viewer so that all three clearly segmented body parts — head, thorax, and abdomen — are simultaneously visible and anatomically legible without any structural occlusion. The entire figure is constructed from the visual language of handcrafted soft clay: every surface is rounded, plump, and gently inflated as though each segment were individually pinched and smoothed by small hands, giving the form a satisfyingly chubby, toy-like solidity that invites touch. The silhouette of the ant is defined by a thick, warm dark-brown outline — not black, but a rich reddish-chocolate brown that reads as a hand-painted contour line, slightly irregular in its edges with the subtle imperfection of real clay modeling, lines uniformly weighted yet carrying the gentle warmth of a handmade object rather than a digital vector stroke.

The head segment is a large, perfectly round sphere sitting atop the thorax, its surface smooth and matte with the characteristic soft sheen of air-dried clay, the top-left face catching the primary studio light source and glowing with a soft warm highlight zone that transitions gradually into a shallow shadow on the right side with absolutely no hard edge or gradient band — just a seamless, velvety light-to-shadow falloff that preserves the matte clay material quality throughout. Two large, perfectly circular eyes sit prominently on the front face of the head, each eye rendered as a glossy glass-bead dome — a tiny convex hemisphere of deep warm brown with a bright white specular highlight dot placed at the upper-left position corresponding exactly to the main light direction, giving the eyes a lively, wet, sparkling quality that immediately communicates friendliness and life. Between and below the eyes sits a small, simple smile — two gentle upward-curving arcs forming a soft closed-mouth expression, the line thin and warm-toned, radiating quiet contentment and approachability. Two antennae extend upward and slightly outward from the top of the head, each antenna a slender curved rod tapering to a small perfect sphere at the tip, the spheres matching the same warm dark-brown clay tone as the body, the antennae positioned symmetrically and angled naturally as though the ant is alert and curious, their tips catching a faint glint of the studio light.

The thorax segment connects directly beneath the head, slightly smaller in diameter than the head but equally rounded and plump, its surface continuing the same smooth matte clay texture, the left-facing surface receiving the primary highlight while the right side settles into a gentle warm shadow. From the thorax extend six legs in total — three on each visible side — each leg composed of three distinct jointed segments rendered as short cylindrical clay tubes with rounded ends, the joints slightly pinched inward to suggest articulation, the legs arranged in the natural alternating tripod gait posture of an insect, the front pair angled forward and downward, the middle pair extending laterally, the rear pair angled backward and downward, all six legs touching the implied ground plane with small rounded foot pads, each leg casting a tiny soft shadow onto the cream background beneath it.

The abdomen segment sits behind and below the thorax, the largest and most bulbous of the three body parts, a wide rounded oval shape that swells generously outward like a well-kneaded ball of clay, its surface the same smooth matte warm dark-brown as the rest of the body, the upper-left curve catching the brightest portion of the studio highlight while the lower-right underside recedes into the deepest shadow zone of the entire figure, this shadow being a soft warm-tinted dark brown rather than cold gray, maintaining tonal harmony with the overall warm palette. A subtle soft drop shadow falls directly beneath the ant onto the cream background — a diffuse, low-contrast shadow with feathered edges spreading gently outward, anchoring the figure to the ground plane and adding dimensional weight without disrupting the clean background.

The lighting is a soft directional studio setup with the key light positioned at the upper-left at precisely forty-five degrees elevation and forty-five degrees horizontal offset, producing a consistent and coherent illumination logic across all three body segments — every highlight appears on the upper-left surfaces, every shadow falls on the lower-right, creating a unified sense of physical presence and three-dimensional solidity. There are no harsh shadows, no specular hotspots beyond the intentional eye highlights, no gradients beyond the gentle light-to-shadow falloff on the clay surfaces, and no secondary colored lights — only the warm, even, enveloping quality of a professional softbox studio environment translated into the matte tactile world of soft clay illustration. The overall color temperature is warm throughout, the cream background harmonizing seamlessly with the reddish-brown clay tones of the ant, the entire image radiating the gentle, safe, inviting emotional register of a premium children's picture book illustration, rendered with ray-traced global illumination, subsurface scattering subtly present in the clay material to give the surface a faint inner warmth, roughness value set high for full matte finish, reflectivity minimal and purely specular at the eye bead level, 8K ultra-high resolution, every clay surface detail, outline imperfection, and shadow edge rendered with extreme fidelity and richness.
